mainTopic: Punishment for leaving Torah, and whether the contents of consecrated items (pit, dovecote, field, tree) are also הקדש
overview: This amud opens by finishing a דרשה on the place-names נפח and מידבא, read as hints to how those who reject Torah are punished. Then רב teaches that one who separates from Torah is consumed by fire, and רבי יונתן teaches that he falls into גיהנם. Each brings a פסוק as proof. Next, the גמרא returns to our משנה, which says that one who sells a dunghill also sells its manure. It compares this to a משנה in מסכת מעילה about consecrated items and what is inside them. If the items were already full when they were consecrated, the contents are הקדש too. If they filled up later, רבי יהודה says the contents are not הקדש. רבי יוסי says the growths of a field or a tree are הקדש. Using רבי's ruling, the גמרא shows that everyone agrees about a pit and a dovecote, and רבה explains a ברייתא the same way. The amud ends with אביי starting a challenge to רבה from the next line of that ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the דרשה: נפח and מידבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the place-names נפח and מידבא as hints to the punishment of those who reject Torah. There are two readings of מידבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Until Nofach" means until a fire comes that does not need fanning. "Until Medeva" means until their souls are pained. Some say it means until God does what He wants with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining a פסוק word by word. It reads two place-names as describing how sinners are punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נפח sounds like ניפוח, fanning a fire, so it hints at the fire of גיהנם, which never needs fanning. מידבא is read two ways. One reading is תדאיב, causing pain to the soul. The other is מאי דבעי, meaning God punishes them however He wishes.

keyTerms.meaning: A place-name in the פסוק, read here as 'fanning'
Blowing on or fanning a fire
A place-name in the פסוק, read here in two ways
Causes pain or grief

phrases.english: "Even until Nofach"
phrases.notes: נפח sounds like ניפוח, blowing on a fire. That is the hook for the דרשה.

phrases.english: means until a fire comes
that does not need fanning,
"until Medeva"
means until their souls are pained.
phrases.notes: Here מידבא is read as if it said מדאיב, causing pain.

phrases.english: And some say it like this:
until He does whatever He wants.
phrases.notes: This time מידבא is read as מאי דבעי, meaning 'what He wants.'

steps.triggerLanguage: עד שתבא אש שאינה צריכה ניפוח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the word-by-word drasha that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נפח hints at the unfanned fire of גיהנם. מידבא hints at pain of the soul, or at God punishing as He wishes.

steps.title: One who leaves Torah is consumed by fire
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that anyone who separates from Torah is consumed by fire, and he brings a פסוק from יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Anyone who separates from words of Torah, fire consumes him. As it says: "I will set My face against them; out of the fire they come, and the fire will consume them."
steps.whatsHappening: Since the דרשה ended with fire, the גמרא brings a related teaching. It says that leaving Torah leads to being burned by fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Torah is compared to fire. 'Out of the fire they come' describes someone who leaves the fire of Torah. 'The fire will consume them' is his punishment. Leaving one fire brings you into another.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates himself or pulls away
Words or matters of Torah
Fire consumes him

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Anyone who separates from words of Torah
fire consumes him,
as it says: "And I will set My face against them;
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 15:7. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: out of the fire they came, and the fire will consume them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יהודה אמר רב כל הפורש מדברי תורה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Linked by the theme of fire as a punishment for rejecting Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who separates from Torah is consumed by fire.

steps.title: One who leaves Torah falls into גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי brings a teaching of רבי יונתן: one who leaves Torah falls into גיהנם, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said that רבי יונתן said: Anyone who separates himself from words of Torah falls into גיהנם. As it says: "A man who strays from the path of understanding will rest in the gathering of the רפאים."
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching makes a similar point with a different פסוק. Leaving Torah leads to גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The path of understanding' is the path of Torah, so straying from it means leaving Torah. He ends up resting among the רפאים. The next step will prove what רפאים means.

keyTerms.meaning: When [a sage] came, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל
The place of punishment for the wicked
The path of understanding, read here as Torah
Spirits or shades of the dead

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
he said that Rabbi Yonatan said:
Anyone who separates himself from words of Torah
falls into Gehinnom,
as it says: "A man who strays from the path of understanding
will rest in the gathering of the spirits."

steps.triggerLanguage: כי אתא רב דימי אמר רבי יונתן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching on the same theme, with a different punishment and a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who separates himself from Torah falls into גיהנם.

steps.title: Proving that רפאים means גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from another פסוק in משלי that רפאים refers to גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רפאים means only גיהנם, as it says: "He does not know that the רפאים are there; those she invited are in the depths of שאול."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the last step by showing that the word רפאים really points to גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק only says the man rests among the רפאים. This second פסוק places the רפאים in the 'depths of שאול,' the underworld. That shows the place is גיהנם, and it completes the proof for רבי יונתן.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is nothing other than; it means only
The underworld
The depths of

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and רבי יונתן teach that leaving Torah brings severe punishment. רב says fire consumes him. רבי יונתן says he falls into גיהנם, proven by linking רפאים to the depths of שאול.

phrases.english: And 'Refaim' means nothing other than Gehinnom,
as it says: "But he does not know that the spirits are there,
those she invited are in the depths of the underworld."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the missing link in רבי יונתן's proof by showing what רפאים means.
steps.raayaObject: That רפאים in משלי 21:16 means גיהנם
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 9:18, which places the רפאים in the depths of שאול

steps.title: Back to the משנה: selling a dunghill
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the legal topic. It quotes our משנה, which says one who sells a dunghill also sells the manure in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One who sold a dunghill has sold its manure, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The אגדה is over, and the גמרא goes back to our משנה. It quotes the line it is about to discuss, so this step opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that when a container-like property is sold, what is inside it comes along with the sale. The גמרא will now look for a related source to compare.

keyTerms.meaning: A dunghill or garbage heap
Manure or dung
Etc.; the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: If he sold a dunghill
he has sold its manure, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה, which also says one who sells a cistern sells its water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah behind and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling a dunghill includes the manure inside it.

steps.title: A משנה from מסכת מעילה: misuse applies to items and their contents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת מעילה. It says that with all kinds of הקדש items, מעילה applies both to the items and to what is inside them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned elsewhere: Anything fit for the מזבח but not for בדק הבית, or for בדק הבית but not the מזבח, or for neither, one is liable for מעילה with them and with what is inside them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another מסכת. It is preparing to connect it to our משנה about selling a dunghill and its contents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three kinds of הקדש: fit only for the altar, fit only for Temple upkeep, or fit for neither. In all three, using them for personal benefit is מעילה. The key new point is that מעילה also covers 'what is inside them,' which is the link to a dunghill and its manure.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
The altar
Upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
One is liable for מעילה, misusing הקדש for personal benefit
What is inside them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'neither for the altar nor for בדק הבית' means the item is not הקדש. It is still הקדש and still has מעילה. It just cannot be used directly, so it is sold and the money goes to the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' is a משנה in מסכת מעילה.

phrases.english: Anything fit for the altar
but not for Temple upkeep;
for Temple upkeep but not for the altar;
neither for the altar nor for Temple upkeep
one is liable for misuse with them
and with what is inside them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנן התם כל הראוי למזבח ולא לבדק הבית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside משנה about items and their contents, to be compared with the dunghill-and-manure rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For all three types of הקדש items, מעילה applies to the items and to their contents.

steps.title: Consecrating items that are already full
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in מעילה explains its rule. If someone consecrates a pit, dunghill, dovecote, field or tree that is already full, מעילה applies to the item and to its contents.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If someone consecrated a pit full of water, dunghills full of manure, a dovecote full of doves, a field full of plants, or a tree loaded with fruit, one is liable for מעילה for using them and for using what is inside them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה from מסכת מעילה, which now gives examples of its rule from Step 6. Every example is an item that was already full at the moment it was consecrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the contents were already there when the item was consecrated, they were included in the הקדש. That is why using either the item or its contents counts as מעילה. This explains the rule from Step 6, the same way our משנה says someone who sells a dunghill also sells its manure.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? This introduces examples that explain a rule.
A dovecote, a structure where doves nest
One is liable for מעילה (misusing הקדש)
A tree loaded with fruit

phrases.english: How so?
If he consecrated a pit full of water;
dunghills full of manure;
a dovecote full of doves;
a field full of plants;
a tree loaded with fruit –
one is liable for misuse with them and with what is inside them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives examples that explain the general rule of the משנה in מעילה quoted in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items that were already full when consecrated: מעילה applies to the item and to its contents.

steps.title: Items that filled up only after being consecrated
steps.stepSummary: If the item was consecrated empty and filled up later, רבי יהודה says מעילה applies to the item but not to its contents.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he consecrated a pit and afterward it filled with water, a dunghill and afterward it filled with manure, a dovecote and afterward it filled with doves, a tree and afterward it grew fruit, or a field and afterward it filled with plants, one is liable for מעילה for using the items, but not for using what is inside them. This is the opinion of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite case, where the contents arrived only after the item was consecrated. רבי יהודה says the contents are not הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is timing. Only what existed at the moment of הקדש became holy. Things that came in later, even growth from the item itself like fruit, are not covered according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And afterward
It became filled

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה applies his rule even to a field and a tree. He holds that fruit or plants that grew later are not הקדש either.

phrases.english: But if he consecrated a pit
and afterward it filled with water;
a dunghill, and afterward it filled with manure;
a dovecote, and afterward it filled with doves;
a tree, and afterward it bore fruit;
a field, and afterward it filled with plants –
one is liable for misuse with them,
but one is not liable for misuse with what is inside them;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הִקְדִּישׁ בּוֹר וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְמַלֵּא מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 7 by covering contents that arrived after the item was consecrated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, contents that come after the item was consecrated are not subject to מעילה, even fruit and plants.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: what grows from a holy field or tree is holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי argues that when a field or tree is consecrated, what grows from it later is also subject to מעילה, because it is growth of הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: If one consecrated a field or a tree, one is liable for מעילה for using them and for using what grows from them, because these are growths of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי יהודה, but only about a field and a tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reason is that the plants and fruit grow out of the holy item itself. Something that grows from הקדש takes on its status. Water in a pit or doves in a dovecote do not grow from the container, so this reason does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Growths, what grows out of something
Growths of consecrated property

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
If he consecrated the field or the tree –
one is liable for misuse with them and with their growths,
because they are growths of consecrated property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה from Step 8, but only for a field and a tree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, growths of a consecrated field or tree are subject to מעילה even if they grew after it was consecrated.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוסי names only a field and a tree. This detail is the basis for the גמרא's question in Step 11.

steps.title: רבי rules: pit and dovecote like רבי יהודה, field and tree like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי, who says רבי יהודה seems right about a pit and a dovecote, and רבי יוסי seems right about a field and a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי said: The words of רבי יהודה seem right for a pit and a dovecote, and the words of רבי יוסי seem right for a field and a tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי decides between the two opinions. He splits them: some cases follow רבי יהודה and others follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As a result, water and doves that come later are not הקדש, while plants and fruit that grow later are הקדש. The way רבי phrases this is what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: The words of this person seem right

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: Just "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.aramaic: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – בְּבוֹר וְשׁוֹבָךְ,
phrases.english: The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem right – for a pit and a dovecote,
and the words of Rabbi Yosei – for a field and a tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A later authority rules on the מחלוקת from Steps 8 and 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pit and dovecote follow רבי יהודה (later contents are not הקדש). Field and tree follow רבי יוסי (later growths are הקדש).

steps.title: Why does רבי's wording suggest רבי יוסי argued about a pit and dovecote?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about רבי's wording. Saying "רבי יוסי seems right about a field and tree" suggests that רבי יוסי argued about a pit and dovecote too, but רבי יוסי only spoke about a field and a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? It makes sense to say "רבי יהודה seems right about a pit and a dovecote," because that implies he argues about a field and a tree, and he does. But saying "רבי יוסי seems right about a field and a tree" implies that he argues about a pit and a dovecote. Yet רבי יוסי only spoke about a field and a tree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רבי worded his ruling. The first half of his statement makes sense, but the second half seems to make up an argument that never existed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you say "X seems right in case A," it suggests X's opinion is not accepted in some other case B, so X must have spoken about B. רבי יהודה did speak about a field and tree, so that half is fine. רבי יוסי never spoke about a pit or dovecote, so the second half of רבי's wording looks unnecessary or wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? An expression that questions a statement
It makes sense that... This sets up the part that is fine before the problem.
By inference, this implies
He disagrees
But look! This introduces a contradicting fact.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not arguing with the ruling itself. It is only asking why רבי worded it in a way that suggests an argument רבי יוסי never made.

phrases.english: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא ״נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּבוֹר וְשׁוֹבָךְ״ –
phrases.english: Granted, "The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem right for a pit and a dovecote" –
this implies that he disagrees about a field and a tree,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא ״נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּשָׂדֶה וְאִילָן״ –
phrases.english: but "The words of Rabbi Yosei seem right for a field and a tree" –
does this imply that he disagrees about a pit and a dovecote?!
But Rabbi Yosei spoke only of "a field and a tree"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רבי's ruling from Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's statement that "רבי יוסי seems right about a field and a tree"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying an opinion seems right in some cases implies that person argued about other cases. רבי יוסי never spoke about a pit or dovecote, so the implied argument does not exist.

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי יוסי was only speaking within רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible answer. Maybe רבי יוסי mentioned only a field and a tree because he was arguing on רבי יהודה's own terms, while he himself holds the same about a pit and a dovecote.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: he was speaking according to the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out of the question in Step 11. This is a setup line, and the very next step will knock it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that רבי's wording makes it sound like רבי יוסי argued about a pit and a dovecote too. The suggestion is that רבי יוסי really does argue there as well. He only mentioned a field and a tree to say: even if you agree with רבי יהודה about a pit and a dovecote, at least admit that a field and a tree are different.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces a suggested answer, often one that gets rejected
According to his words, meaning arguing within the other person's own view

phrases.english: And if you will say:
he (רבי יוסי) was speaking according to the words of רבי יהודה;
phrases.notes: He means: רבי יוסי himself argues even about a pit and a dovecote, but he only pushed back where it was clearest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question about רבי's wording in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of רבי יוסי's statement as argued within his opponent's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי seemed to argue only about a field and a tree.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe רבי יוסי really argues about everything, and named only a field and a tree to argue within רבי יהודה's view (this is rejected next).

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יוסי agrees about a pit and a dovecote
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי saying he disagrees with רבי יהודה only in a field and a tree, because those are growths of הקדש. This implies that he agrees about a pit and a dovecote.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: רבי יוסי said, I do not see the words of רבי יהודה as right in a field and a tree, because they are growths of הקדש. So in a field and a tree he does not see it, but in a pit and a dovecote he does see it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 12 by quoting a ברייתא in רבי יוסי's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reason is that the contents grew out of the הקדש itself. That reason fits only a field and a tree. Water in a pit or birds in a dovecote do not grow from the pit or the dovecote. So רבי יוסי clearly agrees with רבי יהודה there, and he was not just arguing within רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not see, meaning I do not agree
Growths of consecrated property
But, implying the opposite in the other case

phrases.english: But was it not taught: רבי יוסי said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אֲנִי רוֹאֶה דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: I do not see the words of רבי יהודה as correct
in a field and a tree,
because they are growths of consecrated property.
It is in a field and a tree that he does not see it as correct,
but in a pit and a dovecote, he does see it as correct!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַתַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֵין אֲנִי רוֹאֶה דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer of Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי יוסי himself disagrees about a pit and a dovecote
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי's own words and reason (growths of הקדש) show that he agrees about a pit and a dovecote.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once it is clear that רבי יוסי agrees about a pit and a dovecote, the question on רבי's wording comes back stronger, and the גמרא needs a new reading.

steps.title: Rereading רבי: even רבי יוסי agrees about a pit and a dovecote
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי meant that רבי יהודה's view about a pit and a dovecote is accepted even by רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי argued only about a field and a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: the words of רבי יהודה seem right even to רבי יוסי about a pit and a dovecote. Even רבי יוסי argued with him only about a field and a tree, but about a pit and a dovecote he agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 11 by reading רבי's words in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי was not saying that רבי יוסי argued about a pit and a dovecote and lost. He was saying that there is no argument there at all, since even רבי יוסי accepts רבי יהודה's view. The only real disagreement is about a field and a tree.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means: introduces a new reading of a statement
Seem correct
Agrees with him
Disagreed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the names. רבי is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who is weighing the views. רבי יהודה is the תנא whose view about a pit and a dovecote is being accepted.
steps.whatToRemember: About a pit and a dovecote, everyone agrees with רבי יהודה: מעילה applies to the item but not to what filled it later. The only argument is about a field and a tree.

phrases.english: This is what he (רבי) is saying:

phrases.aramaic: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: The words of רבי יהודה seem correct to רבי יוסי,
in a pit and a dovecote –

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֹא נֶחְלַק עָלָיו
phrases.english: for even רבי יוסי did not disagree with him
except in a field and a tree,
but in a pit and a dovecote he agrees with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first answer was rejected, gives the accepted answer to the question of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of רבי's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's wording seemed to describe two arguments, one about a pit and a dovecote and one about a field and a tree.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי means that both sides agree about a pit and a dovecote, so the only argument is about a field and a tree.

steps.title: A ברייתא: dispute about items consecrated empty and filled later
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches a dispute. The תנא קמא says that if items were consecrated empty and filled later, מעילה applies to them but not to their contents. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it applies to the contents too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if he consecrated them empty and afterward they were filled, there is מעילה on them but no מעילה on what is inside them. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: there is מעילה even on what is inside them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a disagreement on the same topic. It sets up רבה's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא does not say which items it means: a pit, a dovecote, a field or a tree. So we need to know how this dispute fits the earlier opinions of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. The next step, from רבה, answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Empty
Were filled
One is liable for מעילה, the misuse of consecrated property

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If he consecrated them empty and afterward they were filled –
one is liable for misuse of them,
but one is not liable for misuse of what is inside them.
רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says:
One is liable for misuse even of what is inside them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הִקְדִּישָׁן רֵיקָנִין וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְמַלְּאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on the same case of items consecrated empty and filled later.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says מעילה applies to the items but not to what filled them later. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it applies to the contents too.

steps.title: רבה: the dispute is only about a field and a tree
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the ברייתא's dispute is about a field and a tree. The תנא קמא follows רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows רבי יוסי. In a pit and a dovecote, everyone agrees that the contents have no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: the dispute is in a field and a tree. The תנא קמא holds like רבי יהודה, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds like רבי יוסי. But in a pit and a dovecote, everyone agrees that there is מעילה on them and no מעילה on what is inside them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains which items the ברייתא is arguing about, and he lines its two sides up with רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits what the גמרא just showed. Since even רבי יוסי agrees about a pit and a dovecote, no one could hold that their later contents have מעילה. So רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון must be arguing only about a field and a tree, where the contents grew out of the הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Dispute
The first opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
Holds like, follows the view of
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: Pit and dovecote: everyone agrees that later contents have no מעילה. Field and tree: רבי יהודה and the תנא קמא say no, while רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון say yes, because they are growths of הקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the whole סוגיא together. There is only one real argument, about a field and a tree, and every source fits into it.

phrases.english: רבה said:
The dispute is in a field and a tree –

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: for the first tanna holds like רבי יהודה,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי;
phrases.english: and רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון holds like רבי יוסי;
but in a pit and a dovecote –
everyone agrees one is liable for misuse of them
and one is not liable for misuse of what is inside them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the scope of the ברייתא's dispute in Step 15 and matches it to the views settled in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's dispute is only about a field and a tree. In a pit and a dovecote, everyone agrees that later contents have no מעילה.

steps.title: אביי brings the next line of the ברייתא, where the view is reversed
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה by quoting the rest of the ברייתא. If the items were consecrated full, מעילה applies to them and their contents, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reverses his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבה: But what about the rest of that ברייתא? It teaches: if he consecrated them when they were full, one is liable for מעילה with them and with what is inside them. And רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reverses his view.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes the second half of the same ברייתא to push back on רבה. This step sets up the challenge; אביי's exact question comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows רבי יוסי, who holds that later growth of a consecrated field or tree is itself holy. In the full case, though, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון flips: he says the contents are not subject to מעילה. אביי is getting ready to ask how that reversal fits רבה's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated them when they were already full
One is liable for מעילה, misusing holy property
What is inside them, their contents
Reverses; flips the ruling around

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In the earlier case (step 15) the items were consecrated empty and filled later. Here they were consecrated already full, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון takes the opposite side.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבה, whose explanation we just saw in step 16.

phrases.english: But what about that which is taught:
If he consecrated them when full,
one is liable for misuse with them and with what is inside them;
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon reverses.
phrases.notes: He flips sides here: when the items were consecrated full, he says the contents are not subject to מעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's explanation in step 16 by bringing the continuation of the ברייתא from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows רבי יוסי regarding a field and a tree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case of items consecrated full, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reverses and exempts the contents. That seems hard to square with following רבי יוסי, who views a consecrated field's growth as holy. The full question continues on the next amud.
